title: Andy's Swiftest Birds
introduction: Andy will tell anyone who lingers by his loft that breeding a racing pigeon is a matter of balancing stubbornness against speed, and he has four birds to prove it. The pigeons are named Alabaster, Nutmeg, Hieronymus and Cadwallader. Each one is entered at a different race distance, and the four distances, listed here from shorter to longer, are 200 miles, 300 miles, 400 miles and 500 miles. Each bird also descends from a different strain: a Delbar, a Janssen, a Stichelbaut and a Sion. Within each of these three lists, every entry belongs to a different pigeon, so each name, each distance and each strain is used exactly once.
clues: Alabaster descends from a Sion and flies 300 miles.
The pigeon that descends from a Delbar does not fly 400 miles.
